what: Behind the screen, a gray cloud mist drifts slowly, and the big colored balls in the four corners (green, lime, teal) bleed into the next color every 2 seconds over 6 seconds, while a few birds fold and spread their wings and cross the screen along a sine curve (8–12s circ.inOut). At first it rises in over 2s as a color mist, then turns gray over 2s, and the fx:color and fx:gray events switch it back and forth between color and gray (color while the menu is open). Color and gray are blended with the original formula 0.5/cos(cos(frame)) − distance×uMotion, so it shimmers subtly every frame (WebGL, three)

options.balls: Corner color orbs, default 1 (four) — 0 means haze only (original subpage)
options.birds: Number of birds crossing, default 3 — 0 means none
options.gray: Time (sec) until it turns gray after floating up, default 2.5 — none keeps it in color
options.fixed: If 0, not attached to the screen and laid only inside the element, default 1
options.--fx-mist-1·2·3: Three colors for the ball and color haze (CSS variables), default --kf-accent · --kf-accent-soft · --kf-line

note: The original mixes a gray and a color video with a shader — here, clouds with the same grain are drawn with fbm noise instead of video. three is received from npm three.cjs as window.exports, placed on window.THREE and called from there

from.where: shared.js stage — fog panel (Qi) · color balls (four rm) · background birds (three As), subpages use balls: 0; birds: 0
